reason: This passage (Exodus 19-32) recounts the golden calf incident. The people explicitly request Aaron to make them gods because Moses delays returning from Mount Sinai. They voluntarily craft and worship the golden calf, directly violating the covenant they had just solemnly agreed to. God explicitly states the people have 'corrupted themselves,' and Moses confronts them saying 'You have sinned a great sin.' The consequences follow directly from their own actions: Moses grinds the calf, scatters it on water, and makes them drink it. The text makes abundantly clear through narrative structure and explicit statements that the people brought judgment upon themselves through willful disobedience. The suffering/consequences (divine judgment, the forced consumption of the calf powder, and spiritual rupture) are the direct result of their own sin.
